text:
Emma (support): ping — AcmeCorp is hitting 401s from our API in their CI pipelines after they rotated their service account token this morning. They say it started at ~08:10 UTC and is blocking every deploy. Error in their logs: 

```
  POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate 401 Unauthorized
  {
    "error": {
      "message": "invalid_scope: token missing required scope inference:invoke"
    }
  }
```

They were using a long-lived CI token created ~6 months ago. They re-created a token via our console and still get the same 401. Any quick triage steps?

Raj (eng-infra): thanks Emma. Two quick clarifying q's: 1) Are they using a service account (bot) token or a user API key from creds page? 2) Do we have the customer org id & token id so I can look up auth logs?

Emma (support): it's a service account token from our Service Accounts page (bot user: acme-deploy-bot). Org: acct-98765, token id they provided: tok_3f8a. They've redacted the token itself. Leo from CS is on the thread with the customer, cc'ing him.

Leo (customer-success): confirming org acct-98765, they rotated the token via our UI and also tried GitHub Actions secrets with the new token — same 401. The customer saw the same request succeed last week. They haven't changed scopes intentionally.

Marta (security): quick heads-up — we rolled out a tighter scope validation change in the auth service yesterday that enforces explicit `inference:invoke` scope on all service-account tokens used against generation endpoints. Intended to be backward compatible with existing tokens, but maybe a migration bug. I'm looking at the deploy.

CI-bot: auth.audit event: org=acct-98765 token_id=tok_3f8a action=validate result=fail reason=missing_scope required=[inference:invoke] timestamp=1748754205

Raj (eng-infra): that matches. Can you paste the token meta we store (masked) for tok_3f8a? I'll check token->scopes mapping and migration run.

Emma (support): from our admin UI (masked): 
```
  token_id: tok_3f8a
  created_by: acme-admin
  created_at: 2025-05-09T14:12:03Z
  scopes: ["read:models", "embed:generate"]  <-- they only had these two
  ttl: 31536000
```

Raj (eng-infra): aha — token did not have `inference:invoke`. That explains 401. Why did this pass before? Marta, did the new validation only start rejecting at enforcement time?

Marta (security): yes, the rollout had a staging phase where we logged missing scopes but still accepted requests. The enforcement toggle flipped to ON at 2025-11-29T08:00:00Z UTC (server config change) to reduce risk surface. We forgot to run the migration that adds `inference:invoke` to existing service-account tokens that had previous generation permissions inferred from role bindings. Going to mark as P0 — this is a regression.

Leo (customer-success): customer impact: blocked deploys for multiple teams at Acme. They're asking for a mitigation ASAP (they cannot create new tokens easily because of internal approval flows).

Raj (eng-infra): short-term mitigation options: 1) temporarily flip enforcement back to 'log-only' for token validation (fast but broad), 2) create a one-off API to inject `inference:invoke` to given token ids (safer, targeted), 3) issue a scoped emergency token for the customer that they can swap in their CI secrets. Which do we want?

Marta (security): prefer option 2 for least blast radius: create admin migration endpoint that grants the missing scope to listed token ids with audit. We'll need an approval from security lead (that's me) and an ops runbook. Estimate ~30-45m if Raj can implement a small migration handler. If we can't do that quickly, option 3 as a stopgap (create ephemeral token with required scope TTL=6h).

Raj (eng-infra): I can push a migration handler to auth service in ~20m if Marta signs off. Will open a PR and a canary to run only for acct-98765 token ids. Also add a safety check: only allow scope additions to service-account tokens that were created prior to enforcement_time and have some allowlist (e.g., had read:models or embed:generate before).

Emma (support): forwarding plan to customer: we'll either patch their existing token or give an emergency token. They want us to try patching first. Please keep me updated so I can coordinate with their SRE.

CI-bot: deploy.status: auth-service/pr-556 merged -> staging canary started (canary targeting acct-98765) at 1748754600

Raj (eng-infra): implemented migration endpoint: 
```
  POST /internal/admin/tokens/patch-scopes
  body: {"token_ids": ["tok_3f8a"], "add_scopes": ["inference:invoke"], "dry_run": false}
```
  ran it for tok_3f8a, response: `{ "patched": ["tok_3f8a"] }` and auth.audit shows success.

CI-bot: auth.audit event: org=acct-98765 token_id=tok_3f8a action=patch result=success added=[inference:invoke] actor=admin-migration timestamp=1748754721

Leo (customer-success): customer verified — their CI job that previously failed now returns 200 and deploy continues. They requested a permanent fix and communication about scope enforcement.

Marta (security): next steps (action items):
- [ ] Rollback plan: we don't need rollback; change is additive.
- [x] Approve migration for affected tokens (done)
- [ ] Add migration to run for all orgs that had token creation date < enforcement_time and tokens missing inference:invoke (owners: eng-infra)
- [ ] Add documentation update for service accounts + token lifetimes + required scopes (owner: docs/devex)
- [ ] Add admin audit endpoint to UI for customer success to request scope patches securely (owner: eng-platform)

Raj (eng-infra): I'll schedule a safe migration run with rate limiting and an allowlist query to avoid touching ephemeral/testing tokens. Also will add a monitoring alert to catch any other orgs who get 401 missing_scope spikes. PR link: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/auth/pulls/556

Emma (support): will message Acme SRE that a permanent migration is planned and that we'll give 24h notice before any mass changes. They asked if token lifetimes are a factor — they use long-lived tokens; Marta, should we recommend short TTLs for CI?

Marta (security): yes recommend short-lived tokens where possible, use rotation via our CLI, or bind tokens to GitHub OIDC where feasible. Also update the least-privilege guidance: service-account tokens should explicitly request only scopes they need (and we should make `inference:invoke` opt-in for generation endpoints in the new docs).

Leo (customer-success): I'll write a customer-facing incident note and link to the support ticket.

Emma (support): closing loop: customer confirmed deploys finished and no further requests failing. I'll keep the thread open until migration run completes org-wide. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Raj (eng-infra): logging postmortem draft headline: "Scope enforcement rollout caused service-account tokens lacking `inference:invoke` to start failing — migration added to restore compatibility" — will ping for reviewers.

Marta (security): tagging for postmortem, include timeline, deploy config change, and why migration wasn't in initial rollout checklist.

CI-bot: incident.bot note: incident created #INC-20251129-0123 linked to thread 1748754321

Emma (support): marking thread resolved for Acme; leaving open for migration follow-up.
